results.title: Inclusion of derived subgroups in free groups (Kourovka 13.62)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The conjecture of V. P. Shaptala that for every free group $F$ and all non-cyclic subgroups $U$ and $V$ of $F$, if the commutator subgroup $[U, U]$ is contained in the commutator subgroup $[V, V]$, then $U$ is contained in $V$.

results.title: Inclusion of derived subgroups does not imply inclusion in free groups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist a free group $F$ and non-cyclic subgroups $U$ and $V$ of $F$ such that the commutator subgroup $[U, U]$ is contained in the commutator subgroup $[V, V]$ but $U$ is not contained in $V$. That is, the conjecture of Kourovka Problem 13.62 is false; the Kourovka Archive credits this answer to M. J. Dunwoody.

results.title: Apostol–Bernoulli numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a complex number and let $\log$ denote the principal branch of the complex logarithm. A sequence $(\beta_k)_{k \ge 0}$ of complex numbers is the sequence of Apostol–Bernoulli numbers $\beta_k(\alpha)$ when $\alpha \ne 0$, $\alpha \ne 1$, and for every complex number $t$ with $|t| < |\log \alpha|$ the series $\sum_{k \ge 0} \beta_k t^k / k!$ converges unconditionally to $t / (\alpha e^t - 1)$.

results.title: Appell sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $R$ be a field of characteristic zero. A sequence of polynomials $(p_n)_{n \ge 0}$ over $R$ is an Appell sequence when, for every $n$, the polynomial $p_n$ has degree exactly $n$ (in particular $p_n \ne 0$) and the formal derivative of $p_{n+1}$ equals $(n + 1)\, p_n$.

results.title: Distinct multiples of $1, \dots, n$ in an interval
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $m$ and $L$, the interval $(m, m + L]$ contains distinct multiples of $1, \dots, n$ when there are pairwise distinct natural numbers $a_1, \dots, a_n$ with $m < a_i \le m + L$ and $i \mid a_i$ for every $1 \le i \le n$.

results.title: Least interval length containing distinct multiples
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, $f(n, m)$ is the least natural number $L$ such that the interval $(m, m + L]$ contains distinct multiples of $1, \dots, n$.

results.title: Lengthening the interval preserves distinct multiples
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $m$, $L$ and $L'$ with $L \le L'$, if the interval $(m, m + L]$ contains distinct multiples of $1, \dots, n$, then so does the interval $(m, m + L']$.

results.title: Some interval contains distinct multiples
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $m$ there is a natural number $L$ such that the interval $(m, m + L]$ contains distinct multiples of $1, \dots, n$.

results.title: The least interval length is admissible
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, let $f(n, m)$ be the least natural number $L$ such that the interval $(m, m + L]$ contains distinct multiples of $1, \dots, n$. Then the interval $(m, m + f(n, m)]$ contains distinct multiples of $1, \dots, n$.

results.title: Characterization of the least interval length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, let $f(n, m)$ be the least natural number $K$ such that the interval $(m, m + K]$ contains distinct multiples of $1, \dots, n$. Then for every natural number $L$, $f(n, m) \le L$ if and only if the interval $(m, m + L]$ contains distinct multiples of $1, \dots, n$.

results.title: The least interval length for $n = 1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, let $f(n, m)$ be the least natural number $L$ such that the interval $(m, m + L]$ contains distinct multiples of $1, \dots, n$. Then $f(1, m) = 1$ for every natural number $m$: the interval $(m, m + 1]$ contains the multiple $m + 1$ of $1$, and the empty interval $(m, m]$ contains nothing.

results.title: Erdős's matching function for multiples in intervals
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $m$, $f(m)$ is the largest natural number $r$ such that for every natural number $N$, every set $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ with exactly $m$ elements and every real $x \ge 1$, there are distinct $a_1, \dots, a_r \in A$ and distinct natural numbers $b_1, \dots, b_r$ in the open interval $(x, x + 2N)$ with $a_i \mid b_i$ for every $i$.

results.title: Statement of Erdős Problem 650
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f$ be Erdős's matching function for multiples in intervals. The statement is the conjunction of four claims: for every natural number $m$, $f(m) = \min(m, \lceil 2\sqrt{m}\,\rceil)$; it is not the case that $f(m) \le \sqrt{m}$ for every natural number $m$; $\sqrt{m} \le f(m)$ for every natural number $m$; and $f(m^2) \le 2m$ for every natural number $m$.

results.title: Sample mean of a data matrix column
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The sample mean of column `j` of an `n × p` data matrix (rows are observations). For `n = 0` it is the junk value `0`.

results.title: Column-centered data matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The column-centered data matrix `X i j - x̄ⱼ`.

results.title: Unbiased sample covariance matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The unbiased sample covariance matrix `(n - 1)⁻¹ (X - x̄)ᵀ (X - x̄)` of an `n × p` data matrix. The divisor needs `2 ≤ n`; for `n = 1` the factor is the junk value `(0 : ℝ)⁻¹ = 0` (and for `n = 0` the product is the zero matrix).

results.title: Principal component scores
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The principal-component scores `(X - x̄) w` of the observations along a direction `w`.

results.title: Centered columns sum to zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The centered columns sum to zero (for at least one observation).

results.title: Entries of the sample covariance matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Entries of the sample covariance matrix: `Sⱼₖ = (n - 1)⁻¹ ∑ᵢ (Xᵢⱼ - x̄ⱼ)(Xᵢₖ - x̄ₖ)`.

results.title: Sample covariance matrix is symmetric
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The sample covariance matrix is symmetric.

results.title: Sample covariance matrix is positive semidefinite
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The sample covariance matrix is positive semidefinite (for every `n`).

results.title: Trace of the sample covariance is the total sample variance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The trace of the sample covariance matrix is the total sample variance, the sum of the column sample variances.

results.title: Principal component scores have sample mean zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The scores along any direction have sample mean zero.

results.title: Sample variance of scores is a quadratic form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The sample variance of the scores along `w` is the quadratic form `wᵀ S w`.

results.title: Eigenvalues of a symmetric matrix in decreasing order
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The eigenvalues `λ₀ ≥ λ₁ ≥ ⋯ ≥ λ_{p-1}` of a real symmetric `p × p` matrix, in decreasing order (Mathlib's `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues` of `Matrix.toEuclideanLin S`).

results.title: Ordered orthonormal eigenbasis of a symmetric matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An orthonormal eigenbasis of a real symmetric matrix, ordered to match `orderedEigenvalues`; for a covariance matrix these are the principal axes.

results.title: Rayleigh quotient of a matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Rayleigh quotient `wᵀ S w / wᵀ w` of a real matrix (junk value `0` at `w = 0`).

results.title: Ordered eigenvalues are decreasing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The ordered eigenvalues are decreasing.

results.title: Ordered eigenbasis vectors are eigenvectors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The `k`-th basis vector is an eigenvector for the `k`-th eigenvalue.

results.title: Quadratic form expanded in the ordered eigenbasis
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The quadratic form expanded in the ordered eigenbasis: `xᵀ S x = ∑ λᵢ ⟪vᵢ, x⟫²`.

results.title: Ordered eigenvalues sum to the trace
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The ordered eigenvalues sum to the trace.

results.title: Eigenvalues of a positive semidefinite matrix are nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The eigenvalues of a positive semidefinite matrix are nonnegative.

results.title: Rayleigh quotient of an eigenvector is its eigenvalue
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Rayleigh quotient of the `k`-th eigenvector is the `k`-th eigenvalue.

results.title: Hotelling's characterization of the principal axes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On nonzero directions orthogonal to the first `k` eigenvectors, the Rayleigh quotient is at most the `k`-th eigenvalue; the bound is attained at the `k`-th eigenvector (`rayleigh_orderedEigenbasis`).

results.title: Lower bound on the Rayleigh quotient for orthogonal directions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Dual of `rayleigh_le_of_orthogonal`: on nonzero directions orthogonal to the eigenvectors after index `k`, the Rayleigh quotient is at least the `k`-th eigenvalue.

results.title: Courant–Fischer min–max, matrix form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every subspace of dimension `p - k` contains a nonzero vector whose Rayleigh quotient is at least `λₖ`.

results.title: Courant–Fischer max–min, matrix form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every subspace of dimension `k + 1` contains a nonzero vector whose Rayleigh quotient is at most `λₖ`.

results.title: Proportion of variance explained by principal components
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proportion of total sample variance explained by the first `k` principal components: `(λ₀ + ⋯ + λ_{k-1}) / tr S` for the sample covariance matrix `S`. The junk value `0` is returned when the total variance `tr S` is `0` (constant data).

results.title: Proportion of variance explained is nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The proportion of variance explained is nonnegative.

results.title: Proportion of variance explained is at most one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The proportion of variance explained is at most one.

results.title: More components explain more variance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Keeping more components explains more variance.

results.title: All components explain all of the variance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: All `p` components explain all of the variance, when the total variance is positive.

results.title: Right singular vectors of a matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Right singular vectors of `A`: an orthonormal eigenbasis of `Aᵀ A`, ordered so that the `i`-th vector has eigenvalue `σᵢ²` with `σ₀ ≥ σ₁ ≥ ⋯` the singular values.

results.title: Truncated singular value decomposition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The rank-`k` truncated singular value decomposition `A Vₖ Vₖᵀ = ∑_{i<k} σᵢ uᵢ vᵢᵀ`, where `Vₖ` collects the first `k` right singular vectors.

results.title: Rank of the truncated SVD is at most k
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The truncated SVD has rank at most `k`.

results.title: Frobenius error of the truncated SVD
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The squared Frobenius error of the truncated SVD is the sum of the discarded squared singular values.

results.title: Eckart–Young (Frobenius norm)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every matrix of rank at most `k` has squared Frobenius distance from `A` at least the sum of the discarded squared singular values.

results.title: Eckart–Young, best-approximation form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The truncated SVD is a best rank-`k` approximation of `A` in the Frobenius norm: the least squared distance from `A` to a matrix of rank at most `k` is `∑_{k ≤ i < n} σᵢ²`, attained by `truncSVD A k`.

results.title: Vanishing family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. A family $F$ of functions on blocks over $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ with values in a type with a zero is vanishing if it is $m$-vanishing for every positive integer $m$.

results.title: The sum-plus-product family $F_c$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $c \in \mathbb{Z}/n$, the family $F_c$ over $\mathbb{Z}/n$ sends a block $(b_1, \dots, b_l)$ of elements of $\mathbb{Z}/n$, of any length $l \ge 0$, to $b_1 + \dots + b_l + c\, b_1 b_2 \cdots b_l$, where an empty sum is $0$ and an empty product is $1$.

results.title: Zero-sum van der Waerden theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every positive integer $n$, the family over $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ sending a block $(b_1, \dots, b_l)$ to $\sum_i b_i$ is vanishing: for every $m > 0$, every sequence over $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ contains $m$ consecutive blocks of a common length $l > 1$, each with sum zero.

results.title: Classification of vanishing for the sum-plus-product family $F_1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n > 1$ and let $F_1$ be the family over $\mathbb{Z}/n$ given by $F_1(b_1, \dots, b_l) = b_1 + \dots + b_l + b_1 \cdots b_l$. If $n \notin \{2, 3, 4, 6, 8\}$, then $F_1$ is not $m$-vanishing for any $m > 0$. If $n \in \{2, 3, 4, 8\}$, then $F_1$ is vanishing. If $n = 6$, then $F_1$ is $1$-vanishing but not $m$-vanishing for any $m > 1$.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $u > 0$ be a natural number and $n = 9u$. Then for every $m > 0$ the sum-plus-product family $F_1$ over $\mathbb{Z}/n$, $F_1(b_1, \dots, b_l) = b_1 + \dots + b_l + b_1 \cdots b_l$, is not $m$-vanishing.

results.title: The sum-minus-product family is vanishing modulo prime powers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, $k > 0$ and $n = p^k$, and let $F_{-1}$ be the family over $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ sending a block $(b_1, \dots, b_l)$ to $\sum_i b_i - \prod_i b_i$. Then $F_{-1}$ is vanishing.

results.title: Vanishing of families of sums of transformed entries
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a positive integer, $d$ a natural number and $g_1, \dots, g_d : \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ maps. Then the family over $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ sending a block $(b_1, \dots, b_l)$ to the vector $\left(\sum_i g_1(b_i), \dots, \sum_i g_d(b_i)\right) \in (\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^d$ is vanishing, where a block counts as vanishing when all $d$ coordinates of this vector are zero.

results.title: Eventual periods of the Fubini numbers modulo an odd number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be an odd natural number and let $\lambda(K)$ be the value of the Carmichael function at $K$. Then a natural number $p$ is divisible by $\lambda(K)$ if and only if there is a natural number $N$ such that the Fubini numbers $F(n)$ satisfy $F(n + p) \equiv F(n) \pmod K$ for all $n \ge N$. In particular, the eventual period of the Fubini numbers modulo $K$ is exactly $\lambda(K)$.

The length of the tour $t$ under $w$ is $\sum_{j=0}^{L-1} w_{t_j, t_{(j+1) \bmod L}}$, the sum of the weights along the closed walk including the return edge from $t_{L-1}$ to $t_0$, where $w_{a,b}$ denotes the entry in row $a$ and column $b$ of $w$, taken to be $0$ when that…

results.title: Well-formed asymmetric TSP instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An asymmetric TSP instance $(n, w, B)$, with $n$ the number of cities, $w$ the weight matrix and $B$ the bound, is well formed when $n > 0$, $w$ has exactly $n$ rows, every row of $w$ has length $n$, and the diagonal entry $w_{a,a}$ in row $a$ and column $a$ is $0$ for every $a < n$.

results.title: Feasible asymmetric TSP instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An asymmetric TSP instance $(n, w, B)$ is feasible when there is a list $t$ of natural numbers with no repeated entries, of length $n$ and containing every $v < n$ (so $t$ lists the cities $0, \dots, n - 1$ in some order), whose tour length under $w$ is at most $B$.

results.title: The asymmetric traveling salesperson decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The asymmetric TSP decision problem accepts a bitstring $x$ when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of asymmetric TSP instances, to an instance $(n, w, B)$ that is well formed and feasible, and rejects $x$ otherwise; in particular it rejects every bitstring that does not decode to an instance.

results.title: TRAVELING SALESPERSON (ASYMMETRIC) is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The asymmetric traveling salesperson decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
